claim: A single proactive face-image forensic watermarking system carrying a 152-dimensional payload can jointly detect deepfake manipulation, localize altered facial regions, and recover a source identifier from both authentic and manipulated images without sacrificing visual fidelity. Detection is measured by the separability of benign and manipulated images, localization by region-level forensic discrepancy scores, source tracing by bit error rate, and imperceptibility by PSNR and SSIM. The bar is a detection ROC AUC above 0.5 with image-level and region-level manipulation decisions made at a 3.2375-pixel discrepancy cutoff, source-tracing bit error rates lower than the strongest prior proactive-forensics baseline under matched conditions, and PSNR and SSIM higher than the strongest prior baseline despite the 152-dimensional payload.

experiments: Build the unified forensic model and its evaluation setup. On CelebA-HQ’s 30,000 images with official splits, resize images to 128×128 and 256×256 and embed a 152-D LIDMark consisting of 136 normalized coordinates from 68 face-alignment landmarks and a 16-D bipolar identifier obtained by truncating a SHA-256 hash of the filename. Pre-train for 100 epochs against Identity, Resize, GausBlur, MedBlur, JpegTest, and JpegMask using Adam, batch size 32, learning rate 4.3×10^-4, and [λ_L,λ_ID]=[11.5,14.7]. Fine-tune for another 100 epochs against SimSwap, UniFace, CSCS, and StarGAN-v2 using batch size 8, learning rate 4.0×10^-4, and [λ_L,λ_ID]=[4.2,1.0], while reserving InfoSwap for testing. Train with one manipulation selected and applied uniformly per mini-batch, using another image in the batch as the source identity for deepfake generation.

Measure whether embedding the 152-D payload preserves visual fidelity. On CelebA-HQ, compare watermarked and cover images by PSNR and SSIM against MBRS, CIN, SepMark, EditGuard, LampMark, DiffMark, and KAD-NET. At 128×128, LIDMark obtains 40.22 dB PSNR and 0.98 SSIM, compared with 40.20 dB and 0.97 for LampMark and 40.12 dB and 0.96 for DiffMark; the baselines carry 30-D payloads while LIDMark carries 152 dimensions. At 256×256, LIDMark obtains 44.31 dB and 0.99, compared with 42.52 dB and 0.95 for LampMark and 41.96 dB and 0.98 for DiffMark; the baselines carry 128-D payloads. Visual comparison of cover and watermarked examples is also reported as showing no discernible artifacts.

Verify that the factorized decoder recovers both parts of LIDMark after ordinary image processing. Apply Identity, Resize, Gaussian blur, median blur, JpegTest, and JpegMask to CelebA-HQ watermarked images, then measure identifier bit error rate and pixel-space landmark Average Euclidean Distance. LIDMark averages 0.27% BER and 1.17-pixel AED at 128×128 and 0.10% BER and 3.06-pixel AED at 256×256. Its BER is 0.00% under Identity, Resize, Gaussian blur, and median blur at both resolutions; JpegTest gives 1.62% and 0.57%, and JpegMask gives 0.00% and 0.01%. The lowest prior average BERs are DiffMark’s 0.46% at 128×128 and KAD-NET’s 0.55% at 256×256.

Test whether intrinsic–extrinsic landmark inconsistency separates benign processing from deepfake manipulation. Recover the embedded intrinsic landmarks with the FHD regression head, independently re-detect extrinsic landmarks from each processed image with the face-alignment library, and compute their pixel-space AED on validation images subjected either to the six common distortions or to SimSwap, UniFace, CSCS, StarGAN-v2, and InfoSwap. Common distortions produce lower intrinsic–extrinsic AED than deepfake manipulations. ROC analysis gives an AUC of 0.9388, and Youden’s J statistic selects 3.2375 pixels as the decision threshold; images with AED above 3.2375 pixels are classified as fake.

Apply the consistency check at facial-region level to localize manipulation. Group the ordered landmark payload by semantic facial component, compute intrinsic–extrinsic AED separately for each region, and label a region manipulated when its AED exceeds the same 3.2375-pixel threshold used for image-level detection. The reported manipulated examples show larger spatial differences between recovered intrinsic landmarks and re-detected extrinsic landmarks in altered regions, while benignly distorted examples retain closer landmark agreement; no aggregate localization accuracy, IoU, precision, recall, or region-level AUC is reported.

Test source tracing after deepfake manipulation. On CelebA-HQ watermarked images processed by SimSwap, UniFace, CSCS, StarGAN-v2, and held-out InfoSwap, decode the 16-D source identifier and compare BER with MBRS, CIN, SepMark, EditGuard, LampMark, DiffMark, and KAD-NET. LIDMark averages 3.33% BER at 128×128 and 2.55% at 256×256, versus the best prior averages of DiffMark’s 3.52% and 2.98%. At 128×128, LIDMark records 0.02% on SimSwap, 0.01% on UniFace, 0.00% on CSCS, 16.42% on StarGAN-v2, and 0.22% on InfoSwap; at 256×256 the corresponding values are 0.97%, 2.44%, 0.01%, 8.47%, and 0.84%. The recovered intrinsic landmark AED averages 1.58 pixels at 128×128 and 4.01 pixels at 256×256.

Check generalization to a deepfake model excluded from fine-tuning. Reserve InfoSwap from the four-model fine-tuning pool, apply it only during testing on CelebA-HQ, and measure recovery of both LIDMark components. LIDMark obtains identifier BERs of 0.22% at 128×128 and 0.84% at 256×256, with intrinsic-landmark AEDs of 1.51 and 3.91 pixels. The lowest prior InfoSwap BERs are LampMark’s 3.35% at 128×128 and DiffMark’s 2.31% at 256×256.

Check cross-dataset generalization without retraining. Apply the CelebA-HQ-trained model directly to 2,000 randomly selected LFW images covering identities and capture conditions unseen in training. LIDMark obtains 39.56 dB PSNR and 0.97 SSIM at 128×128 and 40.68 dB and 0.98 at 256×256. Across SimSwap, UniFace, CSCS, StarGAN-v2, and InfoSwap, its average identifier BER is 4.06% at 128×128 and 2.76% at 256×256, compared with the best prior averages of DiffMark’s 4.66% and 4.50%; its average intrinsic-landmark AED is 1.80 and 4.22 pixels, respectively.

Ablate the two decoder objectives to test their roles in the factorized-head design. At 128×128, disabling landmark loss while retaining identifier loss gives 0.00% BER under common distortions and 0.14% under deepfakes but AEDs of 342.39 and 359.98 pixels; disabling identifier loss while retaining landmark loss gives BERs of 0.42% and 0.49% and AEDs of 2.31 and 2.79 pixels. Joint optimization gives BERs of 0.27% and 3.33% and AEDs of 1.17 and 1.58 pixels. At 256×256, disabling landmark loss gives BERs of 0.00% and 0.29% but AEDs of 540.91 and 405.97 pixels; disabling identifier loss gives BERs of 0.35% and 0.48% and AEDs of 5.29 and 5.65 pixels; joint optimization gives BERs of 0.10% and 2.55% and AEDs of 3.06 and 4.01 pixels.

Test whether the payload can be expanded beyond 152 dimensions. Increase the identifier from 16 to 32 dimensions while retaining the 136-D landmark vector, producing a 168-D LIDMark capable of representing 2^32 identities, and evaluate it at 256×256 on CelebA-HQ. PSNR changes from 44.31 dB for 152 dimensions to 42.36 dB for 168 dimensions, while SSIM remains 0.99. Under common distortions, average BER changes from 0.10% to 0.00% and average AED from 3.06 to 2.19 pixels. Across SimSwap, UniFace, CSCS, StarGAN-v2, and InfoSwap, average BER changes from 2.55% to 3.26% and average AED from 4.01 to 3.01 pixels.

Benchmark the unified model’s computational size against dual-function systems after standardizing watermark length to 152 dimensions. At 128×128, LIDMark uses 5.815M parameters and 12.221 GFLOPs, compared with SepMark’s 28.310M and 4.031 GFLOPs, WaveGuard’s 34.810M and 27.014 GFLOPs, and KAD-NET’s 8.542M and 7.835 GFLOPs. At 256×256, LIDMark uses 21.023M parameters and 60.622 GFLOPs, compared with SepMark’s 28.310M and 16.059 GFLOPs, WaveGuard’s 34.810M and 27.011 GFLOPs, and KAD-NET’s 48.542M and 31.357 GFLOPs.
